S1.rationale: The first-party model Agent repeatedly chooses tools, receives ToolRegistry observations and changes subsequent actions; repeated call detection returns explicit feedback. No independently reproducible failure or open product request is evidenced for the existing S1 path.

S2.rationale: Caller-authored workflows, ConditionalStep rules and nested sequential steps do not introduce a first-party sibling S1 conflict/oscillation regulator. No actual inter-agent collision or accepted demand for native S2 was identified in this library.

S3.rationale: WorkflowExecutor retries, timeouts and events regulate fixed steps rather than live organization-wide resource priorities across S1 cells. The module is a workflow engine, not an incomplete default multi-agent supervisor by definition.

S3*.rationale: The same agent receives tool observations and records event history, without a distinct external source inspector challenging work claims and returning corrective managerial feedback. No native false-success incident justifies an unsolicited reviewer extension.

S4.rationale: Tool/context retrieval and event monitoring affect current tasks but do not autonomously scan prospective external environment or adopt future capability changes. No user-facing improvement hypothesis is justified from the absent S4 label.

S5.rationale: Users construct workflow/model/tool options and runtime permissions, but the installed crate does not own an ultimate identity-policy decision loop. A missing S5 implementation alone cannot ground useful new behavior.
